claims.assertion: RydeX is a non-metered service on which the $6.61 cancellation fee can only stand under NS-0/NS-1, so the whole charge depends on the driver satisfying every element of NS-1.
The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 17:28:05 and was 42 m from the pickup point at that moment, i.e. inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1(i) and (ii) are met — this element is not contested.

After the tap the driver stayed within 200 m for only 4 min 40 s and cancelled at 17:32:45; the earlier approach period from 17:27:05 is excluded from the continuous-wait computation, so the continuous wait after the tap was 4:40 (280 s) and NS-1(iii) is satisfied on its face.

The driver indicated arrival by his own tap (driver_tap) rather than platform auto-detection, and the platform separately logged arrival at 17:27:05 — 60 seconds before the tap — which means the waiting clock Ryde may rely on under NS-1 began at 17:27:05 at the earliest, so the charges rest on records that do not line up with each other.

The only chat message is a single 17:28 driver message announcing his car; there is no message, before the segment, in which the rider agreed to anything, and the rider's statement that she was on her way down is unrebutted by any system record of a refusal to board, so no conduct of the rider waives the fee.

The driver's post-trip statement that he "waited at the pickup" and that the rider "never boarded" is a narrative claim contradicted in part by the system records of F5 and F6, which show arrival logged at 17:27:05 and the tap at 17:28:05; per the record hierarchy the GPS/timeline records govern over the statement.

The rider has 0 disputes and 0 upheld in 90 days over a 1009-day account at 5.0 rating, so there is no pattern of no-shows on her side to support the fee, while the driver carries 1 upheld no-show dispute in the last 90 days.

If the judge reads F5's arrival log as the governing arrival event, the continuous in-radius wait was 5 min 40 s and the fee stands; if the judge reads the driver's own tap at 17:28:05 (F6) as the governing event, the wait was 4 min 40 s and the fee also stands — either way, the rider's contention must rest on the 17:27:05 / 17:28:05 discrepancy being resolved for her, which is the honest weakness of this brief.

No traffic incident was recorded near the route, weather was fair and only a moderate speed band (3, 20–29 km/h) was logged on Lorong 1 Toa Payoh, so nothing in the environment explains an 8 min 45 s pickup sequence ending in a rider-side no-show.

If the judge instead treats the 5 min 40 s approach period as part of the wait, then the wait exceeding the record's threshold is met and the only remaining issue is the unrebutted fact that the booking vanished from the rider's app before cancellation, which supports escalation rather than a finding of rider no-show.

weaknesses: F3 shows the driver stationary for a full 5 min 0 s at 40 m from the pickup and F2 shows 5 min 40 s cumulative inside 200 m, so on the face of the GPS record the driver did wait at the pickup; the rider cannot dispute that she did not board.

F6 confirms the driver pressed "I'm Here" with the record showing 42 m from the pickup at the tap, which meets NS-1(i) and (ii); the only live issue for the rider is whether the 4:40 continuous post-tap wait (F6) is measured from the tap rather than from the earlier platform-logged arrival at 17:27:05 (F5), and if the judge prefers F5 the fee stands under NS-1.

The rider has no system record of the app glitch she complains about (the booking "disappearing"); that assertion rests only on the complaint narrative, which loses to the gps/timeline records (F2–F6) under the record hierarchy.
The 30-day window in NS-7 is not contested by any fact in the table (F4 is the only timing record), and a refund, if any, is a $6.61 voucher rather than cash.

claims.assertion: The driver reached the pickup point and stayed there: GPS puts his closest approach at 4 m from the pickup at 17:27:40 (F1) and a stationary period of 5 min 0 s at 40 m from pickup from 17:27:45 to 17:32:45 (F3), so the vehicle was at the pick-up location within the 200 m arrival radius during the whole wait.

The driver's arrival was confirmed at the pickup (platform/recorded arrival 17:27:05, F5) and his own "I'm Here" tap at 17:28:05 was 42 m from the pickup point (F6), so the NS-1 location requirement at the moment of arrival indication is satisfied.

The driver waited continuously at the pickup well past the 3-minute threshold after the arrival tap: 4 min 40 s within 200 m after the tap (F6) and 5 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m before cancellation (F2), and he only held position until the booking was cancelled at 17:32:45 (F3, F4).

The rider never boarded and never made contact: the chat record is complete with one single timestamped message, the driver's 17:28 message "At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis." (F9, F10), and nothing from the rider, while the driver kept waiting; the cancellation produced the $6.61 no-show fee on record (F7).

There is no GPS gap or uncovered timeline that would displace the no-show finding: the track shows dense, contiguous positions and a continuous 5-minute stationary block up to the cancellation instant (F3), with arrival and cancellation timestamps recorded (F4, F5), so the case is decidable on the system records.

The trip was accepted at 17:24:00 and the pickup area is a HDB Hub / Lorong 1 Toa Payoh corridor running at speed band 3 (20–29 km/h) during 17:19–17:37 (F4, F12), which explains why the driver's approach took until 17:27 — the sequence supports the driver's account that he drove in and waited, rather than the rider's claim that she was still on her way down.

The rider's complaint that the booking disappeared while she was on her way down is contradicted by the system records: the driver was stationary 40 m from the pickup for the final 5 minutes and the fee was recorded as a no-show cancellation (F3, F4, F7), so the $6.61 rider no-show fee stands and no refund is due.

weaknesses: The timeline records 'cancelled by None' with no `cancelled_by` value (F4), so the branch that makes the $6.61 fee payable against the rider (NS-0 / NS-1) rests on inference from the recorded fee rather than an explicit rider-cancellation field — the rider's side will press this.
The rider has a clean record — 5.0 rating, 0 disputes in 90 days, 0 upheld (F15) — so she will be presented as credible and will likely argue she was already en route when the booking vanished.

The driver himself has 1 dispute upheld in the last 90 days, a no-show one (F16); although profile facts cannot decide this case, the rider may use it to argue a pattern and to invite a flag_account under RD-6.

The 17:28 message (F9) only announces the car and colour; it does not demand the rider come down or warn of cancellation, giving the rider room to argue the driver did not chase her actively during the wait.

There is no explicit ETA field in the facts, so the rider cannot be answered with the 'driver late beyond ETA' fairness argument (NS-8); the driver's timely arrival rests on the 17:24:00 acceptance and the 17:27:05 arrival in a band-3 corridor (F4, F12) rather than on an ETA comparison.

points.response: Conceded on location: F1 (closest approach 4 m at 17:27:40) and F3 (stationary 5 min 0 s at 40 m from pickup) do place the vehicle inside the 200 m arrival radius, so NS-1(i)/(ii) location is not contested — but presence alone is not the element that is missing.

This conflates two different arrival events: F5 logs a platform-recorded arrival at 17:27:05 while F6 records the driver's own tap at 17:28:05, 42 m out — NS-1 requires the continuous in-radius wait to run from the arrival indication actually relied on, and the opposing brief switches between the two without resolving which governs.

The two durations are computed from the two different arrival anchors: measured from the driver's tap (F6) the continuous post-tap wait is 4:40, and measured from the 17:27:05 log (F5) it is 5:40 — the driver cannot claim both anchors simultaneously to satisfy NS-1(iii).

D4 is a void claim as framed: it asserts the rider "never made contact" and implies consent-free conduct, but F9/F10 show only one driver message ("At the pickup now, silver Toyota Altis.") with no rider message in evidence at all — absence of a message is not a fact the chat record establishes, and NS-1 turns on the driver's wait, not on the rider's silence.

D5 proves too little for the driver: dense contiguous GPS confirms the vehicle sat at the pickup, but F3's stationary block ending exactly at 17:32:45 also confirms the only thing that happened in the final five minutes — the car did not move and the rider did not board — which is equally consistent with the booking having terminated on the rider's app, as she complains.

F12 shows only a moderate band 3 (20–29 km/h) on Lorong 1 Toa Payoh with no incident logged (F13) and fair weather (F14), so the record explains a slow approach, not an 8 min 45 s sequence ending in a rider-side no-show; F4 fixes acceptance at 17:24:00 and cancellation at 17:32:45.

The premise of D7 fails on F4, which records "cancelled by None" — no cancelled_by value — so nothing in the system records establishes this as a rider no-show cancellation; under NS-0 the $6.61 can only be charged through the rider-cancellation or driver-claims-no-show branches, and the record supports neither on its face, while F15 shows 0 disputes and 0 upheld for the rider in 90 days against the driver's 1 upheld no-show dispute (F16).

Independent of the elements, the record is internally inconsistent on the decisive timestamp (platform arrival 17:27:05 in F5 versus the driver's tap at 17:28:05 in F6) and omits the cancelled_by value (F4); where the record cannot pin the governing arrival event, NS-1's threshold computation is undetermined and NS-7/NS-1 route the fee dispute to human review rather than affirming the charge.

Accepted as far as it goes — the $6.61 stands or falls on NS-1 — but every element of NS-1 is met on the records: tap at 17:28:05 42 m from pickup (F6), a full 5 min 0 s stationary block 40 m from pickup from 17:27:45 to the cancellation (F3), and 4 min 40 s continuous in-radius wait after the tap (F6), which is over the 3-minute default under NS-1(iii).
Conceded: the rider correctly reads F6, and NS-1(i) and (ii) are not in issue.

The rider's own reading gives the driver a 4 min 40 s (280 s) continuous in-radius wait after the tap, which exceeds the 3:01 threshold of NS-1(iii), so the fee is established even on the version of the facts most favourable to her.

There is no contradiction to resolve: NS-1 requires the location condition at the moment the arrival indication is given, and that moment was 17:28:05 with the vehicle 42 m from the pickup (F6), while F5 merely records the platform's earlier arrival confirmation; either timestamp yields a wait longer than 3 minutes before the 17:32:45 cancellation (F4).

No rider consent is needed for a no-show fee — NS-1 rests on the driver's arrival, location and continuous wait, all of which the system records show (F2, F3, F6) — and the complete, timestamped chat containing only the driver's 17:28 message (F9, F10) proves the rider never responded during the wait.

The driver's statement that he waited and that the rider never boarded is not contradicted by F5/F6 but corroborated by them: the track shows 5 min 0 s stationary 40 m from pickup up to the cancellation (F3) and 5 min 40 s cumulative within 200 m (F2), so the record hierarchy favours the driver.

Profile facts cannot decide this case, and in any event F16's single 90-day no-show entry would at most be an additional action under RD-6, not evidence that this particular wait did not happen; the operative facts remain F2, F3 and F6.

The rider's own concession is decisive: on both readings of the arrival event the continuous in-radius wait (4 min 40 s from the tap, F6; 5 min 40 s from the 17:27:05 platform arrival log, F2) exceeds the NS-1(iii) threshold, so neither branch produces a refund.

The environment facts cut against the rider, not for her: the pickup corridor was running at speed band 3, 20–29 km/h, 17:19–17:37 (F12) with fair weather and no incident (F13, F14), which explains an 8 min 45 s pickup sequence (F4) without any failure by the driver, who still held position for the final 5 minutes (F3).

The rider's app-glitch narrative rests only on her complaint and has no system support — the driver was stationary 40 m from the pickup for the last 5 minutes before the 17:32:45 cancellation (F3, F4) and the fee recorded was the no-show cancellation fee (F7) — so there is no evidential gap requiring escalation under NS-7; the records fully decide the case.
